                    ### Question
                    A 16-year-old boy presents to the emergency department after a skateboarding accident. He fell on a broken bottle and received a 4 cm wound on the dorsal aspect of his left hand. His vitals are stable and he was evaluated by the surgeon on call who determined to suture was not required. After several weeks the wound has almost completely healed (see image). Which of the following is the correct description of this patient’s wound before healing?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Incised wound
opb. Abrasion
opc. Laceration
opd. Avulsion
ope. Puncture

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's wound, resulting from a fall on a broken bottle, is characterized by irregular edges and a depth greater than a scrape, indicating tearing of the skin. This aligns with the definition of a laceration, which is a wound caused by blunt force trauma that results in irregular, jagged edges. The reasoning chains correctly identify that the wound does not fit the definitions of an incised wound (clean-cut), abrasion (superficial scrape), puncture (small and deep), or avulsion (complete tearing away of tissue). Therefore, the correct classification of the wound is a laceration.
